title: PRIM vs mutual funds vs PMS: Experts explain how they differ on portfolio structure, costs, taxation and suitability
description: PRIM (Portfolio Managers' Route for Investing in Mutual Fund Units) is a new SEBI framework allowing PMS managers to build portfolios using mutual funds, ETFs.

faq.q: What is PRIM and how is it different from PMS?
faq.a: PRIM (Portfolio Managers' Route for Investing in Mutual Fund Units) is a new offering under the SEBI PMS framework. It differs from conventional PMS by investing solely in direct plans of mutual funds, ETFs, and SIFs, rather than direct stocks or bonds. PRIM has a lower minimum investment of ₹25 lakhs compared to ₹50 lakhs for conventional PMS.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for PRIM?
faq.a: The minimum investment required for PRIM is ₹25 lakhs. This is half the minimum required for conventional Portfolio Management Services (PMS).

faq.q: Are PRIM fees higher than mutual fund fees?
faq.a: Yes, PRIM typically involves a two-layered fee structure. You pay a management fee to the PRIM manager (capped at 1% of AUM), plus the Total Expense Ratio (TER) of the underlying mutual funds, ETFs, or SIFs in which your portfolio is invested. Mutual funds only charge the TER.

faq.q: How does taxation work for PRIM compared to mutual funds?
faq.a: For PRIM, capital gains tax is triggered when the PRIM manager sells units of the underlying mutual funds in your portfolio during rebalancing. For direct mutual fund investments, tax is triggered when *you* redeem the units. The tax rates (STCG/LTCG) follow the rules of the underlying equity or debt funds. [cite: Income Tax India]

faq.q: Can I invest in direct equities through PRIM?
faq.a: No, PRIM is specifically designed for investing in a portfolio of mutual fund units, ETFs, and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs). It does not allow for direct investment in individual stocks or bonds.

faq.q: Who is PRIM best suited for?
faq.a: PRIM is best suited for affluent investors with an investable corpus of ₹25 lakhs or more who seek professional management of their mutual fund portfolio, including expert fund selection, asset allocation, and rebalancing, but prefer diversification through funds rather than direct stock exposure.

faq.q: What are the main benefits of PRIM?
faq.a: The main benefits of PRIM include professional management of your mutual fund portfolio, customised asset allocation, periodic rebalancing by an expert, and a lower minimum investment threshold (₹25 lakhs) compared to conventional PMS, making it accessible to a wider affluent investor base.
